title: Times Reported Hegseth Fired or Sidelined at Least Two Dozen Generals and Admirals
description_short: On Nov. 7, 2025, the New York Times reported that Hegseth had fired or sidelined at least two dozen generals and admirals over nine months, with little explanation.
description_medium: On Nov. 7, 2025, the New York Times reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had fired or sidelined at least two dozen generals and admirals over the previous nine months. It said the actions came with little explanation and described multiple cases. The report also said at least four officers’ promotions had been delayed or canceled because of their previous work with former Joint Chiefs chair Gen. Mark Milley, citing officials.
description_long: The New York Times reported on Nov. 7, 2025, that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had fired or sidelined at least two dozen generals and admirals over the preceding nine months. The article said the actions came with little explanation and based its account in part on interviews with 20 current and former military officials. It described at least four officers whose promotions were delayed or canceled because they had previously worked for former Joint Chiefs chair Gen. Mark Milley, citing officials. The report also described specific personnel cases: Adm. Alvin Holsey stepped down less than a year into a normally three-year assignment after raising questions about deadly strikes on boats in the Caribbean; Lt. Gen. Jeffrey A. Kruse was forced from his post after the Defense Intelligence Agency cast doubt on President Donald Trump’s claim that U.S. airstrikes had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear program. It said Rear Adm. Milton Sands, who had pushed for female instructors in SEAL training, was fired by Hegseth in August. These are examples described in the report, not proof that every affected officer was removed for the same reason. The aggregate remains attributed to the Times; “fired or sidelined” preserves its wording and does not describe all two dozen-plus officers as formally fired.

supported_facts: The Times reported on November 7, 2025, that Hegseth had fired or sidelined at least two dozen generals and admirals over the preceding nine months.
The report said the actions came with little explanation and described interviews with 20 current and former military officials.
The report described delayed or canceled promotions for at least four officers because they had previously worked for former Joint Chiefs chair Gen. Mark Milley, attributing details to officials.
The report described specific cases involving Adm. Alvin Holsey, Lt. Gen. Jeffrey A. Kruse, and Rear Adm. Milton Sands, with the claims attributed to the article and its sources.
quotes: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired or sidelined at least two dozen generals and admirals over the past nine months in a series of ousters that could reshape the U.S. military for years to come.

His actions, which are without precedent in recent decades, have come with little explanation. In many cases, they have run counter to the advice of top military leaders who fought alongside the officers in combat, senior military officials said.

The utter unpredictability of Hegseth’s moves, as described in interviews with 20 current and former military officials, has created an atmosphere of anxiety and mistrust that has forced senior officers to take sides and, at times, pitted them against one another.

Hegseth has delayed or canceled the promotions of at least four senior military officers because they previously worked for Gen. Mark Milley, a former chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff whom President Donald Trump loathes and has repeatedly accused of disloyalty.

Some leaders were ousted for offering candid military assessments. Hegseth soured on Adm. Alvin Holsey, the head of U.S. Southern Command, after he raised questions about deadly military strikes on boats in the Caribbean Sea.

Another senior officer, Lt. Gen. Jeffrey A. Kruse, a 35-year Air Force intelligence officer who led the Defense Intelligence Agency, was forced from his position after his agency cast doubt on Trump’s assertion that U.S. airstrikes in June had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear program.
Rear Adm. Milton Sands, the commander of the Navy SEALs, who pushed to have female instructors in SEAL training, was fired by Hegseth in August.
limitations: This is an attributed news report, not an independent adjudication of each personnel decision or its rationale.
The source uses the combined wording “fired or sidelined”; it does not say that every leader in the aggregate was formally fired.
The specific causal explanations are reported accounts and are not generalized to all affected officers.

rationale: The focused lookup recovered the date-matched November 7 report. It attributes case-specific explanations to the reporting and does not generalize those causes to all affected leaders.
